summary: ObjectGenome mutable-state validation accepts identity aliasing between distinct semantic maps. A state with componentDamage = componentWear validates, after which a wear mutation silently mutates damage. This is a pre-existing ownership/lifecycle defect in the active ObjectGenome hardening lane, not introduced by PR #296's familyVersion identity fix.
evidence: On PR #296 exact head a136f305f432fa9c480e8d91e5d2151340795af7, defaultState(genome) followed by state.componentDamage = state.componentWear is accepted by inspectState because both maps independently satisfy the same component-key and [0,1] value constraints.
After that accepted alias, assigning state.componentWear.shell = 0.5 also changes state.componentDamage.shell to 0.5, coupling two public semantic state channels through table identity.

Docs/OBJECT_GENOME.md specifies a split mutable ObjectState with distinct wear and damage channels; the active audit role explicitly requires ownership/aliasing and mutable-state binding/lifecycle review.

GitHub review 4904204205 records the exact repro and minimal hardening recommendation. Exact-head code CI run 31469830377 is green, so this is an independent semantic contract gap rather than a compiler/lint failure.
